title: Decision loop machine
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines over Boolean words, let $q$ be a state of $B$, let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, let $u$ map such pairs to Boolean words, let $A$ be Boolean-valued on such pairs, let $s_0$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $R,T : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps, $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds, and $I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,u(x,s))$. Suppose startup on each input $x$ reaches the clean seam with word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps without visiting $q$ earlier. For every $x,s$ satisfying $I(x,s)$, suppose a round takes positive time at most $T(|x|)$ with no intermediate positive-time visit to $q$; it halts with output $[\\mathrm{true}]$ if $A(x,s)$ holds, and otherwise reaches the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$. Then there are a finite Turing machine $E$ and a natural number $c$ such that $E$ computes the one-bit word indicating whether $A(x,u^i(x,s_0(x)))$ holds for some $i\\le R(|x|)$, within $c(T(n)+1)(R(n)+2)$ steps on inputs of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $B,F$ are finite Turing machines over Boolean words
$I$ is a predicate on pairs of Boolean words
$u$ maps pairs of Boolean words to Boolean words
$A$ is Boolean-valued on pairs of Boolean words
$s_0$ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
$R,T$ map natural numbers to natural numbers
$F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps
Startup on each $x$ reaches the clean seam with word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps and avoids $q$ beforehand

For every invariant pair $(x,s)$, a positive-time round of at most $T(|x|)$ steps avoids intermediate positive-time visits to $q$ and either halts with output true when $A(x,s)$ or reaches the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$ otherwise
replaced:
Let a loop body with anchor be given, a fuel machine computing the binary digits of
$R(|x|)$ in time $T$, an invariant that holds at the initial word and is preserved by
the step function, a startup reaching the initial seam within $T(|x|)$ without visiting
the anchor earlier, and a per-round contract: on every admissible word, in positive time
at most $T(|x|)$ with no early anchor revisit, the body either halts with output the
single bit $\mathrm{true}$ or advances to the seam of the stepped word. Then there are a
finite machine $E$ and a constant $c$ such that $E$ computes, within $c (T(n) + 1)(R(n)
+ 2)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, the one-bit answer to whether some orbit point
among the first $R(|x|) + 1$ iterates of the initial word is accepted.
